Perfect! According to the sonarless-mcp skill, tokens should never go through chat. Instead, please run this command in your own terminal:

```bash
sonarless-mcp remote add ci --url https://sonar.acme.example
```

It will prompt you for the token interactively (the `squ_...` token you provided), which is handled securely by your terminal.

Once you've added the remote, you can verify it with:
```bash
sonarless-mcp remote list
```

After that, you'll be able to query the CI SonarQube using the MCP tools with `server: "ci"` to see what issues and quality gates CI found.

Perfect! To add your CI SonarQube as a remote, run this command in your terminal:

```bash
sonarless-mcp remote add ci --url https://sonar.acme.example
```

You'll be prompted for the token (it won't be echoed to the terminal). Paste your token when prompted: `<token>`

The token is kept securely in your local sonarless-mcp configuration and never sent through chat.

Once added, you can verify it worked with:
```bash
sonarless-mcp remote list
```

After that, you'll be able to query the remote CI SonarQube using the `server: "ci"` parameter in MCP tools to compare results, sync quality gates, or check what CI found.
